args.summary: Deploy of v2.3.1 to production caused checkout-api to fail health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of 18%. Rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Rollback verified: service healthy again with error rate of 0.2%. Follow-up: investigate the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying.
args.title: checkout-api unhealthy after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0 in all regions

trace.final:
Done. Here's what happened:

1. **Diagnosis**: Deploy of **v2.3.1** to production was failing health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate. The most recent healthy production release was **v2.3.0**.
2. **Rollback**: Rolled all production regions back to v2.3.0. Verified — service is healthy again with error rate down to 0.2%.
3. **Incident**: Opened **SEV2 incident INC-0001** (on-call paged) documenting the failed v2.3.1 deploy, the rollback to v2.3.0, and verification that the service recovered. The incident notes a follow-up to investigate v2.3.1 before any redeploy.

Note: I did not redeploy v2.3.1 — per policy, deploying a version that has never been healthy in production would require change-manager approval, and it's currently failing anyway.
